reason: B proposes the more physically plausible high-temperature wear mechanism: formation, retention, and regeneration of an oxide tribolayer can govern friction and material loss, and atmosphere-controlled wear tests with oxide characterization provide a direct test. A relies on the unsupported premise that annealing will refine this coating and create stable nanotwins, then conflates dislocation blocking with suppression of grain-boundary sliding at 500–600 °C.
